extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users (mathematicians, category-theory students) needing to typeset commutative diagrams
extracted.subtask_description: A practical overview helping LaTeX users choose and learn packages for drawing commutative diagrams, aimed at readers from beginners to advanced users working in category theory or related mathematical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a package based on your level of needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Milne ... provides a nice one-page quick overview description of several available packages with some very good practical advise to users depending on the level of their needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a package suited to your experience and the complexity of diagrams you need: for quick/simple needs pick lightweight/easy packages; for complex/custom diagrams prefer more powerful packages. (The page refers readers to Milne's guidance for concrete mappings from user needs to package choices.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer modern packages (include TikZ among options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feruglio's 1994 overview names many primary packages but 'misses a few of the more modern packages including TikZ.' Milne's list includes tikz (Tantau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surveying options, ensure modern alternatives such as TikZ/TikZ-CD are considered — they may offer better current support and functionality than older packages listed in older surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for long and detailed user guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Naturally, just reading through some of the 20+ page user guides to some of these packages can be quite daunting...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect steep documentation; allocate time to read package manuals and tutorials. Consider starting with shorter introductions or one-page overviews (e.g., Milne) before tackling full user guides. Avoid being discouraged by documentation length; look for concise tutorials (linked on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult comparative overviews and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Gabriel Valiente Feruglio has a nice overview article naming all the primary packages with some compare/contrast information ... He lists them alphabetically and gives brief overviews of some of the functionality of each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use meta-overviews (Feruglio, Milne) to compare packages' strengths/weaknesses before diving into package-specific docs. Comparative articles help narrow choices quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider community/expert recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: David Spivak ... seems to prefer XY-pic, diagXY, and TikZ based on his website from which he links to guides to each of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor in the preferences and published workflows of experienced practitioners (e.g., textbook authors) when choosing a package, since their choices reflect practical tradeoffs for mathematical diagramming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize 'bigger' / well-documented packages for advanced needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the recommendations given in several of the resources above, I’ve narrowed the field a bit to some of the better sounding packages. I’ve provided links to the packages with some of the literature supporting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For feature-rich or production-quality diagrams prefer packages with substantial documentation and community resources — examples listed: Diagxy (Michael Barr), XY-pic (Kristoffer Rose & Ross Moore), Diagrams (Paul Taylor), TikZ-CD (Florêncio Neves). Follow package manuals, CTAN pages, and tutorials linked on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CTAN package pages and package manuals/tutorials
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for some of the 'Bigger' Packages: Diagxy: Michael Barr (CTAN Package, Brief four page introduction); XY-pic: CTAN Package, XY-pic User Guide; Diagrams: CTAN Package, Diagrams Manual; TikZ-CD: CTAN Package, TikZ-CD Package Documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or learning a package, read its CTAN page, official user guide, and available tutorials/examples. The page lists specific manuals and tutorial articles (with authors and dates) to consult for each major package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask for recommendations / community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a particular package you recommend? Feel free to add your thoughts, comments, and additional resources in the comments below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure which package to choose, solicit opinions and example workflows from peers or online communities (e.g., blog comments, StackExchange). Real-world examples and user experiences can reveal practical pros/cons not obvious from manuals.
